title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous pages): M is a free Z/4Z-module of rank 2, i.e. the 4-torsion of an elliptic curve in characteristic ≠ 2. M_0 = M/2M ≅ F_2^2, and J = M_0^* is the set of 3 nonzero vectors, equivalently P^1(F_2). M^* is the set of primitive vectors, and Δ_M = M^*/{±1} = P(M)(Z/4Z) is a 6-element set. The degree-2 reduction map Δ_M → J gives Δ_M the structure of the vertex set of an octahedron whose 3 diagonals are the fibres. Under this structure the combinatorics translate as follows:
- faces are the sections of Δ→J;
- edges are the partial sections over 2-element subsets of J;
- vertices are the partial sections over 1-element subsets;
- incidence is extension of sections, i.e. inclusion of subsets of Δ.

On this page:
(1) G = GL(M) = GL_2(Z/4), of order 96, acts on Δ by octahedral automorphisms. The kernel of the action is the scalar group ζ = {±1}. Check: if g = 1+2X fixes every line, then X is scalar mod 2, giving g = ±1. Hence there is an injection GL(M)' = GL(M)/{±1} = PGL_2(Z/4) → Aut_oct(Δ). Both groups have order 48 = 24×2, so this is an isomorphism (33): PGL_2(Z/4) ≅ Aut_oct(Δ) ≅ Aut^+(Δ) × {1, a_Δ} ≅ S_4 × Z/2. Here a_Δ is the antipodal map, which generates the centre. The marginal NB identifies GL(M)' with the projective group GP(M); this works because the units of Z/4 are ±1.
(2) Computation of the centre of GL(M)'. The centre of GL(M_0) ≅ S_3 is trivial, so the centre lies in the kernel K = (1+2End(M_0))/{±1} ≅ End(M_0)/F_2·id. This is an 8-element F_2[S_3]-module ≅ M_0 × F_2. The centre is therefore the S_3-invariants of K, namely F_2[ω]/F_2. Here F_2[ω] = {0, 1, X, X^2} ≅ F_4 is the canonical subring of End(M_0) generated by the order-3 elements of GL_2(F_2).
- Check: X = [[1,1],[1,0]] satisfies gXg^{-1} ∈ {X, X+1 = X^2} for all g, so its class is invariant. M_0 has no S_3-invariants.
- The central element 1+2X sends each primitive v to v+2Xv. Since Xv ∉ {0, v}, this is the other point of the same diagonal, i.e. the antipodal map, consistent with (33).
(3) The page ends by starting the description of an octahedron with diagonal set J as a torsor under F_2^J; the next page identifies the set of faces with P_M/ζ.

Purpose: a canonical, coordinate-free dictionary between level-4 structures (Z/4-modules of rank 2) and octahedra. It is a tool for the moduli of elliptic curves with level structure in characteristic ≠ 2, e.g. understanding the action of PGL_2(Z/4) ≅ S_4×Z/2 on X(4) and its 6 cusps.
errors: No mathematical errors. Orders (96, 48), kernel {±1}, the isomorphism with the full octahedral group S_4×Z/2, and the centre F_4/F_2 ≅ Z/2 (acting as antipodism) all check out.
Minor notational slip or ambiguity: the bracketed '/β={±1_{M_0},1_{M_0}}' should be the quotient by F_2·id_{M_0}, corresponding to the scalars {±1} of GL(M).

ideas.what: P^1(Z/4) is the vertex set of an octahedron, with diagonals the fibres of reduction to P^1(F_2); faces, edges and vertices are total and partial sections.
ideas.modern_name: Octahedral structure of P^1(Z/4Z); cusps of X(4) as octahedron vertices (Klein's octahedral picture of level 4)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Klein (1870s–1890s, Klein–Fricke) for the octahedral level-4 picture; the sections formulation is a folklore reformulation
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses Platonic solids/regular maps and dessins in general terms; this specific level-4 dictionary is not known to be published

ideas.what: GL_2(Z/4)/{±1} = PGL_2(Z/4) is isomorphic to the full octahedral group S_4 × Z/2, proved by injectivity plus order count.
The centre of PGL_2(Z/4) is the image of 1+2F_4, i.e. (1+2F_2[ω])/{±1}, and acts as the antipodal map.
ideas.modern_name: Centre of PGL_2(Z/4Z) via S_3-invariants in End(F_2^2)/scalars

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, canonical treatment of classical facts: the octahedral structure of P^1(Z/4), PGL_2(Z/4) ≅ S_4×Z/2, and the centre as F_4/F_2 acting by antipodism. It is a pleasant intrinsic presentation, but nothing here would be new to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: 'F_2^ω' is most likely F_2[ω] (≅ F_4, ω a cube root of unity), the subring of End(M_0) generated by an order-3 element; both occurrences.
'β={±1_{M_0},1_{M_0}}' should read as the quotient by F_2·1_{M_0}, i.e. '/F_2.1_{M_0}'.
First lines: 'les sommets s'identifient aux sections partielles sur des parties de J réduites à un élément — la relation d'incidence avec celle de prolongement des sections' (J, not I).
'et ce qui est là le noyau' should read 'et que c'est là le noyau de l'opération'.
Last line: 'La donnée d'un octaèdre Δ ayant J comme ens. des diagonales équivaut à celle d'un torseur' (J, not I).
'G_J ≃ Gl(M_0)' / 'S_J ≃ Gl_{F_2}(M_0)': the index should be J, not I.
